sections.title: 55.1 Hierarchical budget allocation
sections.body:
A parent agent must not delegate its full remaining budget independently to every child.

Suppose the parent has \$0.10 remaining and creates five subagents.

If each receives a \$0.10 allowance, the actual potential expenditure becomes \$0.50.

Parent task budget

# \$0.10

```svg
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 35" width="100%" height="35px" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M150 0 V15 H50 V35 M150 15 V35 M150 15 H250 V35" stroke="#64748b" fill="none" /></svg>
```

Parent reserves remaining \$0.02 for aggregation and verification.

The invariant is:

\[
\sum ChildReservations+ParentReservation
\leq AvailableBudget
\]

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments. If each receives a \$0.10 allowance, the actual potential expenditure becomes \$0.50.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

sections.title: 55.2 Distributed cost reservation
sections.body:
Use atomic reservations with a durable ledger:

```sql
UPDATE tenant_budget
SET reserved_microusd =
    reserved_microusd + :estimate
WHERE tenant_id = :tenant_id
  AND spent_microusd
      + reserved_microusd
      + :estimate
      <= limit_microusd
RETURNING reserved_microusd;
```

Persist a unique reservation record in the same database transaction.

After execution:

- Settle actual provider usage.
- Release unused reservation.
- Record ambiguous provider billing separately.
- Reconcile against provider billing reports.

If actual expenditure can exceed the estimate, reserve conservatively, enforce model output limits and define overrun handling.

steps.label: Input
steps.narration: Untrusted input enters the system and must be classified before use.

steps.label: Policy check
steps.narration: Security and tenancy policies decide what is allowed.

steps.label: Model
steps.narration: The model runs inside a trust boundary with constrained tools and prompts. If actual expenditure can exceed the estimate, reserve conservatively, enforce model output limits and define overrun handling.

steps.label: Output filter
steps.narration: Outputs are scanned for leakage, jailbreaks, and policy violations.

steps.label: Audit
steps.narration: Every sensitive decision is logged for investigation and compliance.

sections.title: 55.3 Cost of multi-agent delegation
sections.body:
Suppose:

- Single-agent execution costs \$0.012 and succeeds 80% of the time.
- Multi-agent execution costs \$0.030 and succeeds 95% of the time.

| Architecture | Cost per successful task |
|--------|--------|
| Single agent | \$0.015 |
| Multi-agent | \$0.03158 |

The multi-agent system is more accurate but more expensive per successful task.

For high-value business tasks, the accuracy improvement may justify the cost. For low-value FAQs, it may not.

diagram.title: Visual flow — 55.3 Cost of multi-agent delegation

steps.label: Orchestrator
steps.narration: A coordinator decomposes work and assigns ownership to specialists.

steps.label: Delegate
steps.narration: Tasks are handed off with clear inputs, outputs, and termination conditions.

steps.label: Specialists
steps.narration: Specialist agents execute narrow skills and return structured results.

steps.label: Merge
steps.narration: Results are reconciled; conflicts and duplicates are resolved before final output.

steps.label: Terminate
steps.narration: The workflow must always end — via success, safe failure, timeout, or human decision.
